steps.action: Open Settings: click the extension icon, choose Manage in the popup header, then open the Settings tab in the Manager window.
steps.expected: The Settings panel opens and checks this installation's identity.
steps.visualCue: Manage button in the popup header.

steps.action: If the identity notice appears, enter your name and choose Register.
steps.expected: The current API key is labeled with your name and future or historical shared links are attributed to you.
steps.visualCue: Identity notice at the top of Settings.
steps.tip: If Email account host was already configured, the extension derives and registers your name automatically.

steps.action: Pick a theme variant — Dark, Slate, Light, Cream, Nord, Dracula, Rosé, or Tokyo Night.
steps.expected: Every extension surface re-colors instantly.

steps.action: Set 'Email account host' to your own account name.
steps.expected: Your From identity is configured.
steps.warning: Power Automate sends remain blocked while this required value is blank.

steps.action: Write your email signature in the signature editor.
steps.expected: Signature saves; it will auto-append to Power Automate sends.

steps.action: Review Settings → Features and switch off anything you won't use.
steps.expected: Disabled features vanish from shelves, popups, and shortcuts immediately.
steps.tip: Everything except Power Automate is on by default. Leaving it all on is fine.

steps.action: (If your team shares config) paste its URL under Settings → Shared Settings Templates and select Preview.
steps.expected: The template name and included scopes appear; tick only the scopes you want and import them.
steps.commonMistake: Importing the Settings scope overwrites your theme and toggles — untick scopes you want to keep your own.

tutorials.title: Send your first templated email
prerequisites: On a CRM page (order, case, contact, or account)

steps.action: Click the extension icon in Chrome's toolbar.
steps.expected: The popup opens showing templates matched to this page type.
steps.commonMistake: 'No templates' usually means no template of this page's type exists, or its rules don't match — check the Template Editor.

steps.action: Pick a template from the dropdown.
steps.expected: The RESOLVED section streams in live values from the page — name, order number, totals.
steps.visualCue: RESOLVED list below the dropdown; unresolved variables stay highlighted.

steps.action: Scan the resolved values, then click Send.
steps.expected: With Power Automate on: sends silently with your signature. Otherwise: a pre-filled Outlook window opens.
steps.visualCue: Send button in the popup footer.
steps.tip: Treat a highlighted (unresolved) variable as a stop sign — fix it before sending.

tutorials.title: Log a call and create a follow-up task
prerequisites: On a contact or account page

steps.action: Double-tap Shift. Choose Call <name> to dial and open the logger, or Log incoming call to open it without dialing.
steps.expected: Call Log opens showing the contact's name and phone, with the template filter focused.

steps.action: Type to filter call templates; press a number key or Enter to pick one — or press '/' to compose from scratch.
steps.expected: The composer pre-fills; '/' walks you through category → direction → voicemail → subject → note.
steps.visualCue: Live preview pane updates as you type.
steps.tip: The entire flow works without the mouse — Enter advances each field.

steps.action: Submit the call log.
steps.expected: Success confirmation; the call is in the CRM activity log.

steps.action: Open Quick task for <name>, pick a template, and set the due date.
steps.expected: Use Today, Tomorrow, In 3 days, Next week, or enter a date as mm/dd/yy.

steps.action: Submit the task.
steps.expected: Task attaches to the contact in the CRM with your category, priority, and due date.

tutorials.title: Build & send a product proposal
prerequisites: On a contact, account, or order page

steps.action: Double-tap Shift and click Gift Catalog.
steps.expected: The catalog opens with the product grid and category sidebar.
steps.commonMistake: No shelf? Check actionsShelfEnabled in Settings → Features.

steps.action: Search a product name or browse the category sidebar.
steps.expected: The grid filters live; a Custom Logo group sits at the top.
steps.tip: First open after 24 hours re-indexes the whole site — a short delay is normal.

steps.action: Click Customize on an item.
steps.expected: The customize panel opens with the imprint types this product actually supports.

steps.action: Pick Logo, Text, or Monogram; optionally enable the second pole.
steps.expected: The live 3D ball updates with your artwork.
steps.visualCue: 3D preview on the right — drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.

steps.action: (Optional) choose a Gift Set package.
steps.expected: The 3D preview swaps to the assembled open box; pricing recomputes with the gift-set ladder.

steps.action: Set the quantity and review the price ladder.
steps.expected: Per-unit price updates at volume breaks.
steps.warning: The margin guardrail flags prices under your minimum margin (default 30%).

steps.action: Click Add to Quote; repeat for more items.
steps.expected: The proposal sidebar fills with line items and a running total.

steps.action: (Optional) apply a promo code.
steps.expected: Discount or free-item lines appear; only applicable promos are offered.

steps.action: Click Email Proposal.
steps.expected: The composer opens with rendered line items and 3D snapshots of each customized product.
steps.visualCue: Snapshots render automatically — give it a second.

steps.action: Review recipient, subject, and body, then Send.
steps.expected: Confirmation toast; the proposal is saved server-side, tracked, and the opportunity value updates.
steps.commonMistake: If Outlook opened instead, Power Automate is off — see 'How Email Sending Works'.

tutorials.title: Triage a case email
prerequisites: On a contact page with Case Email History

steps.action: Click the preview button on an email row.
steps.expected: The full thread opens inline — messages in order, images included.
steps.visualCue: Button appears on hover over the row.

steps.action: Read the thread; expand any collapsed quoted sections.
steps.expected: Quoted replies unfold in place.
steps.visualCue: Collapsed sections marked in the thread.

steps.action: Click the recommended category chip (or press 1–9).
steps.expected: Category and subcategory apply to the case.

steps.action: Use the recommended reply template to start a draft.
steps.expected: A reply opens pre-filled with the best-matching template.
steps.tip: Recommendations come from your template rules — better rules, better suggestions.

steps.action: Open the Actions Shelf and choose Manage order dates.
steps.expected: The Order Date Manager opens with two mini-calendars.
steps.visualCue: Smart actions for the current order.

steps.action: Pick the approval date on the left calendar, the commitment date on the right.
steps.expected: Selected dates show in the readouts under each calendar.

steps.action: Click Update Dates.
steps.expected: A step-by-step progress toast walks the save; it confirms when both dates are committed.
steps.commonMistake: If a step fails, the toast names it. Nothing half-saves — re-open and retry. Repeated failure at step one means your admin session expired; reload the page.

tutorials.title: Extract a logo & submit a proof
prerequisites: On an order page with artwork

steps.action: Hover the product/render image and click the expand button.
steps.expected: The Image Viewer opens and resolves the best-quality original (direct file → express upload → CDN → render fallback).
steps.visualCue: Floating button appears over the image on hover.
steps.tip: Shift+click the button to download the logo immediately, skipping the viewer.

steps.action: Zoom and pan to inspect the artwork; download or copy the URL if needed.
steps.expected: Crisp original artwork, not the page's cropped render.

steps.action: (Optional) open the color-swap popover → Mockup Composer to recolor and render a 3D grass-scene mockup.
steps.expected: Recolored logo renders on a 3D ball, ready to download.

steps.action: Click Submit Proof.
steps.expected: The form opens with order and customer IDs pre-filled and the image carried over.

steps.action: Pick the item and artist, add notes, submit.
steps.expected: The proof posts to the CRM and appears in the gallery of prior proofs.

tutorials.title: Run a bulk workflow
prerequisites: Power Automate strongly recommended for real sends

steps.action: Press Ctrl+K, search or apply a saved query, and tick the rows you want.
steps.expected: A selection summary bar appears with workflow actions.
steps.tip: Build the audience as a saved query first (Query Builder) so you can verify and reuse it.

steps.action: Click Run Workflow.
steps.expected: Workflow Manager opens with the selected rows loaded as the audience.
steps.visualCue: Audience count in the top bar.

steps.action: Choose a saved workflow or create one, then add and configure its steps.
steps.expected: The timeline shows each email, task, call, or custom step in execution order.
steps.visualCue: Step cards in the center timeline.
steps.commonMistake: Use Email selected—not Run Workflow—when you only want the separate Quick Send bulk-email panel.

steps.action: Click Simulate and inspect at least one selected contact.
steps.expected: The trace shows conditions, routing, resolved templates, and planned actions without CRM writes.

steps.action: Turn on Dry run and click Dry run.
steps.expected: The full selected audience is processed with zero emails sent and zero CRM writes.
steps.visualCue: Dry run status and audience progress.
steps.tip: Review several contacts before a live pass; it is the cheapest QA available.

steps.action: Turn Dry run off and click Run workflow.
steps.expected: The workflow runs once for each selected account or contact, with live progress and pause/resume controls.
steps.warning: Keep Chrome open until the run completes.

tutorials.title: Import supplier products
prerequisites: For SnugZ: signed in to snugzusa.com in another tab

steps.action: Open the custom items panel and start an HPG or SnugZ import.
steps.expected: The importer pages the supplier catalog and filters to customizable products.
steps.visualCue: Import buttons in the custom items repo UI.

steps.action: Let it fetch detail pages for the filtered products.
steps.expected: Costs, options, minimums, and lead times populate with a progress indicator.
steps.warning: Large imports fetch many pages — don't navigate away mid-run.

steps.action: Review the computed markup and price ladders.
steps.expected: Each product shows its cost ladder and your sell-price ladder.

steps.action: Select the items you want and save.
steps.expected: They land in your custom items library (deduped by SKU), ready to add to proposals.
steps.visualCue: Items appear with a source tag.

steps.action: Settings → Shared Settings Templates → Create URL; name the template and choose scopes.
steps.expected: The extension stores only the chosen scopes on RevStack and creates a revocable opaque URL.
steps.visualCue: Scope checklist in the create dialog.
steps.tip: For a team template pack, tick only template scopes and leave Settings out so people keep their own theme and toggles.

steps.action: Copy the generated URL and send it to the intended teammate.
steps.expected: No JSON file is created; the URL identifies the server-side template.

steps.action: Teammate: paste the URL, select Preview, choose scopes, then Import.
steps.expected: Templates merge by id (same id replaces, new id appends); settings scopes overwrite.
steps.commonMistake: Importing Settings replaces the teammate's theme/toggles. Server-managed policy remains independent and is reapplied on sync.

steps.action: On an order (or contact) page, click the extension icon and choose Watch Order or Watch Contact.
steps.expected: A small add form appears with the current record pre-linked.
steps.visualCue: Watch button beside Watch List in the popup.

steps.action: Give it a title, priority, and optional due date, then add.
steps.expected: The item lands on your Watch List with a link back to the order.

steps.action: Open Watch List any time to review; tick items done as they resolve.
steps.expected: Filter chips show live counts; completed items auto-clean after 5 days.
steps.tip: Watch List is local and private — use Quick Task instead when the team needs to see the follow-up in the CRM.

steps.action: Press Ctrl+K, then click the filter button.
steps.expected: The Query Builder opens.
steps.visualCue: Filter icon next to the search bar.

steps.action: Add conditions: pick a field, an operator, a value. Group them with AND/OR.
steps.expected: Example: state is TX AND (order count > 5 OR YTD > 2000).

steps.action: Click Apply.
steps.expected: Results update to the matching contacts/accounts.

steps.action: Click Save and name the query.
steps.expected: It appears in your saved queries for one-click reuse — and as a workflow audience.
steps.tip: Verify the audience visually here before ever pointing a workflow at it.

tutorials.title: Handle a notification
prerequisites: A new update is available for this extension installation

steps.action: Open the extension popup and choose Notifications.
steps.expected: The Unread tab lists new updates and its count matches the toolbar badge.

steps.action: Search by title, message, or topic if needed.
steps.expected: The list narrows without changing read state.
steps.visualCue: Search field below the Unread / All / Archived switcher.

steps.action: Choose the notification action, or mark a message read.
steps.expected: A registered action opens the relevant tool; Mark read removes only the unread badge.
steps.visualCue: Action link inside the row and check button on hover.

steps.action: Archive an update you no longer need in the current list.
steps.expected: It moves to Archived and remains available as offline history.

tutorials.title: Apply an order note
prerequisites: At least one note template exists, or you have text for a custom note

steps.action: Open the Actions Shelf and choose Apply order note.
steps.expected: Quick Order Note opens with the template filter focused.
steps.visualCue: Contextual order action near Manage order dates.

steps.action: Pick a saved note, or enter composer mode and fill Audience, Subject, and Body.
steps.expected: The preview contains exactly what will be posted.
steps.visualCue: Audience must match an option from the order page.

steps.action: Review any Push dates forward value, then choose Apply.
steps.expected: The note posts through the order-notes iframe; configured date movement runs through the date-push chain.
steps.warning: A failing date-push step is reported by name; do not assume the date moved until success appears.

steps.action: For an unchanged repeat, use Apply last note the next time the shelf opens.
steps.expected: The most recently applied saved template posts without reopening the picker.
steps.visualCue: Apply last note only appears after a saved-template application.

tutorials.title: Use a custom CRM workspace
prerequisites: The relevant Contact, Account, or Opportunity takeover is enabled under Settings → Custom Pages → CRM

steps.action: Open a Contact Details, Account Details, or Opportunity Details record.
steps.expected: The registered extension workspace replaces the stock detail page for that page only.
steps.visualCue: Metric cards and focused data sections replace the legacy CRM layout.

steps.action: Review the record sections and open the related task, activity, email, order, proof, contact, or proposal you need.
steps.expected: Links and actions retain the current record context.
steps.visualCue: Each workspace exposes a different set of sections appropriate to its record type.

steps.action: On Contact Details, use the standalone composer for a normal template email; on Opportunity Details, use proposal selection/breakdown for quote work.
steps.expected: The operational email or proposal flow opens with the record context supplied.
steps.visualCue: Do not use the Contact composer's saved-proposal slash command; it is marked Not implemented yet.

steps.action: If you need the stock page, turn off only that takeover in Settings.
steps.expected: The stock CRM page returns without deleting CRM records or extension-local data.

tutorials.title: Scan My Clients for recent orders
prerequisites: A saved Query Builder query named exactly My Clients

steps.action: Open CRM Search with Ctrl/Cmd+K, then expand the Actions Shelf.
steps.expected: CRM Search's modal-specific actions join the shelf.
steps.visualCue: Run last query and Scan for recent orders.

steps.action: Choose Scan for recent orders.
steps.expected: The saved My Clients audience is searched for orders since the prior scan; the first run covers seven days.
steps.visualCue: Progress and result count appear in CRM Search.
steps.commonMistake: A differently named query is not used. Save it as exactly My Clients.

steps.action: Inspect the results before selecting, exporting, emailing, or starting a workflow.
steps.expected: Only the records you intentionally select move into a bulk action.
steps.visualCue: Selection summary appears after checking rows.

steps.action: Run the scan again on a later day.
steps.expected: It continues from the successful local watermark instead of repeating the original seven-day window.
steps.visualCue: Advanced recovery: __gbScan.status() inspects the clock; __gbScan.reset() clears it.
